materials.title: L6 본문 (Dr. Schofield)
materials.text: On February 28, 1919, a man came to Dr. Schofield’s house. A man: Dr. Schofield, I have a special favor to ask you. Dr. Schofield: What can I do for you? A man: Many people are going to gather tomorrow for the independence of Korea. Could you take pictures of the event and share them with the world? At 2 p.m. on March 1, Dr. Schofield was hiding in a building and saw a large group of people gathering outside. He began to take pictures. Dr. Schofield: Unbelievable! There are so many people here. I hope the world will learn about this important event through my pictures. Do you know Seok Hopil? His English name was Frank W. Schofield, but he loved his Korean name. It sounded similar to his real name, and it also had a good meaning. Dr. Schofield was a Canadian doctor, and he first came to Korea in 1916 to teach medicine. He wanted to teach in Korean, so he began to learn Korean right away. He studied so hard that he was able to teach in Korean after only a few years. He believed that every country has the right to be independent, so he helped the Korean independence movement. On March 1, 1919, Dr. Schofield heard people shouting for Korean independence in Tapgol Park. He took pictures of the event with his camera. He then wrote an article about the historic event and sent it to foreign newspapers with his pictures. Dr. Schofield’s fight for Korean independence didn’t stop even after the March 1st Movement. He continued to write about the terrible situation in Korea for foreign newspapers. He was under the watchful eye of the Japanese police, so he had to go back to Canada in 1920. In 1958, he returned to Korea at the invitation of the Korean government and never left again. For the rest of his life, he worked hard to help Koreans, especially poor students. Dr. Schofield died in April 1970, and he was buried in Seoul National Cemetery.

materials.title: 외부지문 Yu Gwansun
materials.text: Yu Gwansun showed her love for her country with courage. She was only a teenager when Korea was under Japan's control. Even though she was young, she believed she could do something with her courage. On March 1 in 1919, she bravely stood up and joined others to fight against Japan's control over Korea. She told her friends and neighbors not to give up hope. Although she faced many challenges, she never gave up. She was caught for her actions and had a difficult time in prison. However, even then, she stayed strong and hopeful and continued to inspire people around her. Her love wasn't loud or forceful but was full of kindness and care. Yu Gwansun's story teaches us that anyone, even a young person, can show great courage and deep love. It reminds us to fight for our rights and stay brave during challenging times.

materials.title: 외부지문 Homer B. Hulbert
materials.text: Homer B. Hulbert was an American educator, writer, and missionary who truly believed in the future of Korea. He first came to Korea in the late 1800s to teach at a royal school, but his work quickly went beyond the classroom. Hulbert noticed that the Korean writing system, Hangeul, was logical and easy to learn. While many Westerners didn't care about it, Hulbert praised Hangeul and studied it deeply. He believed that promoting Hangeul and Korean culture could make the people stronger. When Japan began taking control of Korea, Hulbert didn't keep quiet. He wrote in international newspapers to say Korea should be free. He also traveled to the U.S. and Europe to tell people about Korea and ask for independence. His actions made him a trusted friend to many Koreans. Even after he left Korea, Hulbert continued to help the Korean independence movement. He returned to Korea in his later years and died in Seoul in 1949. Today, he is remembered as a foreigner who loved Korea with deep respect. Hulbert's story teaches us that true friendship and love can go beyond countries.

materials.title: A Doctor with a Korean Name (밑줄 ①~⑤)
materials.text: Seok Hopil is the Korean name of a Canadian doctor ①[whom Koreans still remember] today. He came here to teach medicine, and he practiced Korean every evening with his students. In fact, he studied ②[so hardly that] he could teach his classes in Korean in only a few years. On the first day of March in 1919, he ③[heard a huge crowd shouting] for freedom near Tapgol Park. The pictures ④[which he took] on that day soon traveled to foreign newspapers. There ⑤[used to be] very few foreigners who told the world the truth about Korea, so his articles were precious.

materials.title: My Hero Report (수업 과제물)
materials.text:
My Hero Report — Class 2-3, Kim Jimin

Last week our class learned about people who fought for Korean (A)__________. For my report I chose a foreign doctor. He was under the watchful eye of the police, but he still wrote an (B)__________ about the terrible situation in Korea and sent it to a newspaper in his own country. He believed that every country has the (C)__________ to be free. Years later he came back at the invitation of the Korean government and never left again. I used to think that only Koreans worked for our country, but the story of this doctor was so moving that I changed my mind.

items.stem_ko:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 낱말로 알맞은 것은? (P1의 본문 어휘)

the state of being free and not controlled by another country
options: invitation
movement
independence
situation
government
items.why_ko: 다른 나라의 지배를 받지 않고 자유로운 상태는 independence(독립)이다. invitation(초청), movement(운동), situation(상황), government(정부)는 풀이와 맞지 않는다.

items.stem_ko: T1의 대화 [1]~[5] 중 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 부분이 어법상 틀린 것은?
options: ①
②
③
④
⑤
items.why_ko: used to 뒤에는 동사원형이 오므로 used to played가 아니라 used to play가 되어야 한다. ①은 so ~ that, ③은 지각동사+목적격보어(-ing), ④는 목적격 관계대명사, ⑤는 too ~ to 구문으로 모두 올바르다.

items.stem_ko: T3의 ①~⑤ 중 어법상 어색한 문장은?
options: ①
②
③
④
⑤
items.why_ko: too는 that절과 함께 쓰이지 않는다. so heavy that I couldn't lift it 또는 too heavy for me to lift로 써야 한다.

items.stem_ko:
우리말과 뜻이 같도록 주어진 단어를 바르게 배열한 것은?

나는 어제 누군가가 내 이름을 부르는 소리를 들었다.
(heard / someone / calling / I / my name / yesterday)
options: I heard someone called my name yesterday.
I heard someone to call my name yesterday.
I heard someone calling my name yesterday.
I heard calling someone my name yesterday.
I heard my name someone calling yesterday.
items.why_ko: 지각동사 hear는 목적격보어로 동사원형이나 현재분사를 쓴다. 진행 중인 동작을 나타내므로 hear+someone+calling이 알맞다. to부정사(②)나 어순이 뒤바뀐 ④⑤는 틀리다.

items.stem_ko: P1의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
options: He liked his Korean name because it sounded similar to his real name and had a good meaning.
He first came to Korea in 1916 to teach medicine.
He learned Korean because he wanted to teach his students in Korean.
He left Korea in 1920 because the Korean government asked him to leave.
He died in April 1970 and was buried in Seoul National Cemetery.
items.why_ko: P1에서 그는 일본 경찰의 감시를 받고 있었기 때문에 1920년에 캐나다로 돌아가야 했다. 한국 정부는 오히려 1958년에 그를 초청했다.

items.stem_ko: T2의 대화 [1]~[5] 중 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 부분이 어법상 틀린 것은?
options: ①
②
③
④
⑤
items.why_ko: 목적격 관계대명사 that이 이미 목적어 역할을 하므로 뒤에 목적어 it을 다시 쓸 수 없다. that everyone likes로 써야 한다.

items.stem_ko: P1에서 Dr. Schofield가 말한 this important event가 가리키는 것으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
options: 캐나다 의사가 의학을 가르치러 한국에 처음 온 일
1919년 3월 1일에 사람들이 한국의 독립을 위해 모인 일
Dr. Schofield가 한국어를 배우기 시작한 일
한국 정부가 Dr. Schofield를 한국으로 초청한 일
Dr. Schofield가 서울 국립묘지에 안장된 일
items.why_ko: 건물에 숨어 사진을 찍으면서 한 말로, 3월 1일에 한국의 독립을 위해 많은 사람이 모인 사건을 가리킨다.

items.stem_ko: T4의 ①~⑤ 중 어법상 어색한 문장은?
options: ①
②
③
④
⑤
items.why_ko: 지각동사 see는 목적격보어로 to부정사를 쓰지 않는다. saw a boy cross 또는 saw a boy crossing으로 고쳐야 한다.

independence – essay – right
independence – article – courage
independence – article – right

items.why_ko: (A) 한국의 '독립'을 위해 싸운 사람들 → independence, (B) 신문에 보낸 '기사' → article, (C) 자유로울 '권리' → right. have the right to ~ 구문이다.

items.stem_ko: T8의 (A), (B), (C) 괄호 안에서 어법상 알맞은 것끼리 짝지어진 것은?
options: such – shout – which
so – shout – which
so – to shout – which it
such – to shout – which
so – shout – which it
items.why_ko: (A) 뒤에 형용사 brave가 오므로 so ~ that, (B) 지각동사 heard의 목적격보어는 동사원형 shout, (C) 목적격 관계대명사 뒤에는 목적어 it을 다시 쓰지 않는다.

items.stem_ko: P2의 대화 내용과 일치하는 것은?
options: Somi decided to write her essay about Dr. Schweitzer.
Liam recommended Audrey Hepburn to Somi.
Somi is looking for books about famous scientists.

items.why_ko: Liam은 Somi에게 Audrey Hepburn을 추천했고, Somi는 그녀에 대해 쓰기로 했다. 그녀는 남을 도운 유명한 사람들에 관한 책을 찾고 있으며, Amy는 이탈리아 음식을 좋아한다.

items.stem_ko: T5의 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?
options: ①

items.why_ko: P3에서 가장 좋은 방법은 버스를 타는 것이고 2번이나 5번 버스로 약 10분이 걸린다. 그림에는 의자 두 개와 큰 탁자가 있고, 얼굴 사진은 거리에 붙이며, 조부모는 지금 도시에 살며 일하지 않는다.
